title: Dating the Start of Coverage on a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan
content:
Coverage comes into force on the date the plan's effective date rule produces from the day the plan received the completed election form, and never on any other date.

**Condition of record.** CMS has returned an accepting transaction reply code for this enrollment and that code is recorded on the enrollment record. The enrollment record is the authority, tested before the coverage is brought into force and matched on the enrollment reference.

**The dating rule.** Under the rule carried by every Ridgecrest Advantage plan, an election received in any month takes effect on the first day of the next month. An election made in the annual election period takes effect on 1 January of the following contract year however early in the period it was received. An initial coverage election takes effect on the first day of the month in which the member's Part B entitlement begins.

**Retroactive effectuation.** Retroactive effectuation is made only where CMS directs it, and then only back to the number of months the plan held allows; the plan never chooses a retroactive date to suit the member's claims.

**Rejection.** Where CMS rejects the transaction the enrollment is not effectuated, the member keeps whatever coverage they had, and the rejection reason is explained to them in plain words.

**What bringing coverage into force does.** It mails the member identification card and opens the first premium charge; it never opens a premium charge for a month before the coverage effective date.

### Dating cases

| Circumstance | Date coverage comes into force |
| --- | --- |
| Completed election form received on 3 April, outside the annual election period | 1 May |
| Completed election form received on 30 April, outside the annual election period | 1 May |
| Completed election form received on 18 October, inside the annual election period | 1 January of the following contract year |
| Completed election form received on 6 December, inside the annual election period | 1 January of the following contract year |
| Initial coverage election, Part B entitlement beginning 1 July | 1 July |

The two annual election period rows show that the date of receipt inside that period does not move the start date: both produce 1 January of the following contract year. The first two rows show that a form received on the first day and on the last day of one month produce the same start date, the first day of the month after it.
